analysis: Both units are base-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 1031-1535, historical release notes). The PR change to this file is documentation only: the head side adds roughly 800 lines for a v0.10.6 candidate, which also covers two-Mac cluster rollout notes. The patch excerpt is truncated, and the supplied units hold only pre-existing base text, so the new head content was not fully visible to me. I found no executable code, configuration or workflow change in these units. Nothing in the base excerpts regresses any threat-model control, such as the T-041 prefix-cache posture, the TB-011 App Attest authorization boundary, the A-008 token custody or the TB-012 add-on hold socket. The historical notes only restate existing behavior, including the relaxed installer signature check for dev/staging versions (an existing pre-release-only exception), the release registration flow and the SSD checkpoint staging caps. The visible patch excerpt describes cluster runtime facts carried in release registration as `cluster_runtime`, with platform-side derivation of cluster approvals. That is a new trust surface: pair serving over Thunderbolt/RDMA, new inter-Mac traffic, the coordinator deriving grants from release-supplied claims, and plaintext handling across two Macs. It is described only in the truncated head excerpt and is outside the supplied source units, so the actual cluster code was not reviewed. The next pass should check that the cluster transport authenticates peers and encrypts or protects prompt data (A-001, TB-003, TB-007), that pair approvals cannot be self-asserted by a provider, that cluster-mode serving respects App Attest authorization (A-016, T-053), and that the threat model gets a trust-boundary entry for the Thunderbolt cluster. Because the cluster code is not visible here, I make no finding and flag deeper review.
